## What it is

Eclipse Mosquitto is a small open-source MQTT broker (MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1). Sensors, Zigbee2MQTT, Home Assistant, Node-RED and scripts publish messages to *topics* on it and subscribe to the topics they care about, so devices on the home network can talk to each other without knowing about each other ([mosquitto.org](https://mosquitto.org), [README](https://github.com/eclipse-mosquitto/mosquitto/blob/v2.1.2/README.md)). It has no web UI in this package: clients connect over MQTT on port **1883**.

**Licence:** `EPL-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause`, dual-licensed under the Eclipse Public License 2.0 or the Eclipse Distribution License 1.0, which is BSD-3-Clause ([LICENSE.txt at v2.1.2](https://github.com/eclipse-mosquitto/mosquitto/blob/v2.1.2/LICENSE.txt)). The image's `org.opencontainers.image.licenses` label gives the same expression. GitHub reports `NOASSERTION` for the repository. The research licence matrix (`research-output/evidence/license-matrix.csv`, row "Eclipse Mosquitto (default MQTT 5 app, W8-R1)") writes it as `EPL-2.0 OR EDL-1.0 (BSD-3-Clause)`. `EDL-1.0` is not an SPDX identifier, so that row does not match the SPDX expression above, and the licence gate cannot confirm the licence. Until the matrix row uses `EPL-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause`, the gate classes the app `blocked`. Under the BSD-3-Clause option this is class L1 (permissive).

**Version:** upstream publishes no GitHub releases, only tags. `v2.1.2` is the latest tag (annotated, tagged 2026-02-09; [ChangeLog.txt](https://github.com/eclipse-mosquitto/mosquitto/blob/v2.1.2/ChangeLog.txt) "2.1.2 - 2026-02-09").

**Image:** `docker.io/library/eclipse-mosquitto`, the Docker Official Image built from the upstream [docker/2.1-alpine](https://github.com/eclipse-mosquitto/mosquitto/tree/v2.1.2/docker/2.1-alpine) Dockerfile. For 2.1.2 only the `2.1.2-alpine` tag exists. The index also has arm/v6, 386, ppc64le and s390x images; the manifest declares amd64 and arm64.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials, not the Eclipse Mosquitto logo.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`, 1 replica) and a `ClusterIP` Service `mosquitto` on port **1883** (MQTT, no TLS). In-cluster clients use `mosquitto.app-mosquitto.svc:1883`.
- **No anonymous access.** The image's default config (`docker/2.1-alpine/mosquitto.conf`) allows anonymous access on 1883 and opens an HTTP dashboard listener on 9883. This package replaces it with the ConfigMap `mosquitto-config` (`manifests/mosquitto.conf`): `allow_anonymous false` and no dashboard listener.
- **Users** come from the [Dynamic Security plugin](https://mosquitto.org/documentation/dynamic-security/). Its config is `/mosquitto/data/dynamic-security.json`. From 2.1, when that file does not exist, the plugin generates it on first start with the users `admin` (administers users and roles) and `democlient` (read/write on `#`), with random passwords stored in plain text in `dynamic-security.json.pw` (see First run).
- **Persistence:** the `persist-sqlite` plugin stores retained messages and persistent sessions in `/mosquitto/data` (upstream [docker README](https://github.com/eclipse-mosquitto/mosquitto/blob/v2.1.2/docker/2.1-alpine/README.md), "Configuration"). Everything lives on the 1 GiB PVC `mosquitto-data`. Logs go to stdout.
- It runs as UID/GID 1883, the `mosquitto` user that the upstream Dockerfile creates, not as root. It also runs with a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, all Linux capabilities dropped and the default seccomp profile. The image has no `USER`: its entrypoint runs as root only to `chown` the data directory. Here, `fsGroup: 1883` gives the process the volume instead.
- Probes: TCP on 1883 for readiness and liveness. MQTT has no HTTP health endpoint.

**Sizing:** upstream publishes no sizing. In the smoke test (k3s, arm64) the broker used about 4 MiB of memory idle, with an 8 MiB peak. Requests are 25m CPU and 32Mi; the 128Mi limit leaves room for many clients and retained messages.

**Smoke test:** the gate's HTTP smoke check does not apply because there is no web port. On a throwaway k3s (Lima, 2026-11-12), these checks passed by hand:
- rollout ready;
- anonymous and wrong-password connections refused (`not authorised`);
- `democlient` published a retained message with the generated password, and it was still delivered after a pod restart;
- `mosquitto_ctrl dynsec` changed the admin password, created a client, deleted `democlient`, and the new client could publish.

## First run

Source: [Dynamic Security plugin, "Generating the configuration file - 2.1 onwards"](https://mosquitto.org/documentation/dynamic-security/) ([source at v2.1.2](https://github.com/eclipse-mosquitto/mosquitto/blob/v2.1.2/www/pages/documentation/dynamic-security.md)), and `man mosquitto_ctrl`.

1. Install Eclipse Mosquitto from the Market and approve the action. It installs into the namespace `app-mosquitto`.
2. Read the generated passwords. The file is plain text, and upstream says to delete it once the passwords are known:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-mosquitto exec deploy/mosquitto -- cat /mosquitto/data/dynamic-security.json.pw
   ```
3. Set your own admin password. `mosquitto_ctrl` does not prompt for the password it connects with, so pass the generated admin password with `-P`. It then asks for the new password twice:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-mosquitto exec -it deploy/mosquitto -- mosquitto_ctrl -u admin -P '<admin password>' dynsec setClientPassword admin
   ```
4. Create one client per device or app, give it the `client` role (read/write on all application topics), then remove the demo user. Use the new admin password with `-P`; `createClient` asks for the new client's password:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-mosquitto exec -it deploy/mosquitto -- mosquitto_ctrl -u admin -P '<admin password>' dynsec createClient zigbee2mqtt
   kubectl -n app-mosquitto exec deploy/mosquitto -- mosquitto_ctrl -u admin -P '<admin password>' dynsec addClientRole zigbee2mqtt client
   kubectl -n app-mosquitto exec deploy/mosquitto -- mosquitto_ctrl -u admin -P '<admin password>' dynsec deleteClient democlient
   ```
   For narrower access, create roles with `mosquitto_ctrl dynsec createRole` and `addRoleACL` (see the same page).
5. Delete the plain-text password file:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-mosquitto exec deploy/mosquitto -- rm /mosquitto/data/dynamic-security.json.pw
   ```
6. Point clients at `mosquitto.app-mosquitto.svc:1883` with their username and password. To test from your machine: `kubectl -n app-mosquitto port-forward svc/mosquitto 1883:1883`, then `mosquitto_sub -h localhost -u <user> -P <password> -t '#' -v`.

## Not done yet

- **No TLS listener.** Passwords cross the network in clear text, and `mosquitto_ctrl` warns about it. Keep the broker inside the cluster or home network. TLS (port 8883) needs a certificate, which OneMind does not issue to apps yet.
- **Not reachable from outside the cluster.** Devices on the LAN (ESP32 sensors, for example) need a LoadBalancer or NodePort Service, which this v0 package does not create.
- The upstream HTTP dashboard (port 9883) is not enabled.

**Hold (apps/market-unblock-2, 2026-11-13):** Not a vulnerability: the licence-matrix row says `EDL-1.0`, which is not an SPDX id, so the licence gate cannot confirm it. The fix is a one-line row in `research-output/evidence/license-matrix.csv`, outside `apps/` and outside this change. Licence-blocked apps stay blocked.
